learn.title: Final mixed-domain revision
objectives: Bring together all three AZ-900 domains in mixed, exam-style questions.
Tell apart the services and concepts most often confused on the exam.
Answer scenarios that combine two ideas, such as a region and a redundancy option, or a policy and a lock.
Pick out the keyword in a question that points to the right answer.
concepts: Consumption model
No upfront cost. Pay for what you use, and stop paying when you remove it.
Shared responsibility
Microsoft always owns the physical layer. You always own your data, devices, and accounts and identities.
IaaS / PaaS / SaaS
VMs (you manage the OS) / App Service, SQL Database (you manage the app and data) / Microsoft 365 (you just use it).
Region, zone, pair
Region = geography with datacenters. Zone = separate datacenters inside a region. Pair = two regions in one geography used for disaster recovery.
Hierarchy
Management group > subscription > resource group > resource. Policy and RBAC are inherited downward.
Storage redundancy
LRS (one datacenter), ZRS (three zones), GRS (LRS plus a secondary region), GZRS (ZRS plus a secondary region). The RA- versions add read access to the secondary.
Blob tiers
Hot, Cool (30 days), Cold (90 days), Archive (180 days, offline, must be rehydrated).
VPN Gateway vs ExpressRoute
VPN Gateway is encrypted over the internet. ExpressRoute is a private connection that doesn't cross the public internet.
Entra ID, RBAC, Conditional Access
Entra ID handles who you are (authentication). RBAC handles what you can do on Azure resources (authorisation). Conditional Access sets if/then sign-in rules.
Zero Trust
Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach.
Azure Policy vs locks
Policy controls what can be created or how it's configured. Locks stop deletion or changes, even by Owners.
Tags
Name-value pairs for organising and allocating costs. They aren't inherited by default; Azure Policy can apply them.
Pricing calculator vs Cost Management
The calculator estimates costs before you deploy. Cost Management analyses, budgets and alerts on actual spending.
Advisor, Service Health, Monitor
Advisor makes recommendations. Service Health reports Azure incidents and maintenance that affect you. Monitor collects your metrics and logs, and alerts on them.
Azure Arc
Manage and govern servers and Kubernetes clusters outside Azure as if they were Azure resources.
comparisons: Scalability vs elasticity
Scalability means you can add or remove resources. Elasticity means it happens automatically with demand.
High availability vs disaster recovery
High availability keeps a service up through small failures. Disaster recovery restores it after a major outage.
Availability set vs availability zone
A set spreads VMs across racks in one datacenter (99.95%). Zones spread them across datacenters (99.99%).
Container Instances vs AKS vs Container Apps
Container Instances is the simplest single container. AKS is managed Kubernetes orchestration. Container Apps is serverless microservices that can scale to zero.
App Service vs Functions
App Service hosts web apps that are always running. Functions runs event-driven code, billed per execution.
Blob Storage vs Azure Files
Blob Storage is object storage reached over HTTP. Azure Files is an SMB or NFS file share you can mount.
AzCopy vs Storage Explorer vs File Sync
AzCopy is a command-line tool. Storage Explorer is a graphical tool. File Sync caches Azure Files shares on Windows Server.
Azure Migrate vs Data Box
Azure Migrate discovers, assesses and moves servers. Data Box ships large data offline on a physical device.
Microsoft Purview vs Azure Policy
Purview governs data (discovery, classification, compliance). Azure Policy governs resource configuration.
Public vs private endpoint
A public endpoint is reachable over the internet. A private endpoint gives the service a private IP address inside your virtual network.
traps: A deallocated VM still charges for its disks.
Data transfer into Azure is free; data transfer out generally isn't.
Resource locks apply to Owners too.
Tags don't flow down from resource groups unless a policy makes them.
A resource group can't contain another resource group, and each resource is in exactly one resource group.
Not every region has availability zones or a paired region.
Serverless still runs on servers. You just don't manage them.
Azure Advisor recommends changes; it doesn't apply them automatically.
Azure AD is now Microsoft Entra ID.
The pricing calculator gives estimates, not bills, and needs no Azure account.
revision: Cloud concepts is 25–30% of the exam, architecture and services 35–40%, and management and governance 30–35%.
Read each scenario for the deciding keyword: 'without managing servers', 'automatically', 'prevent deletion', 'before deploying'.
Physical security is always Microsoft's job. Data and identities are always yours.
A zone protects you from a datacenter failure. A second region protects you from a region failure.
RBAC permissions are cumulative and are only ever allowed. Policy can deny.
Use Cost Management budgets to get alerts. Use tags to allocate costs.
Use Service Health for Azure's problems and Monitor or Application Insights for your app's problems.
ARM templates and Bicep are declarative IaC. Every request goes through Azure Resource Manager.
A pass is 700 on a scale of 1 to 1,000.

questions.on: Define cloud computing

Services are delivered over a network
You can provision resources on demand
